evidence:
STATIC STRUCTURE (frozen task .qc-cache/hireops-lessons-2026-10-08-r5/task):
(1) Reward formula: tests/scoring.toml, tests/tools/score.py and tests/test.sh are byte-identical to the frozen template (diff empty). Gates render/constraints = 0.0 with all_pass; weights functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2; floor functional 0.05 (strict >). score.py sets reward to the weighted mean only if every gate > 0 and functional > 0.05, else 0. The weighted mean of per-dimension weighted means is monotone non-decreasing in every criterion score; gate and floor thresholds are monotone step functions. Function (0.6) outweighs craft (0.4 total), so the skill's 'craft carrying more mass than function' inversion is absent.
(2) Gates: tests/gates/render/judge.toml:24-26 (wrong password refused, then correct sign-in shows a usable workspace) and tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:63-65 (UI add on the seeded Data Analyst job, reload, Observer reads it in an independent context). Both are basic load/reload/server-backed prerequisites that any conforming app meets (instruction.md:19, hireops_rules.md s1-s2; Data Analyst exists in seed with interview_limit 2). No gate demands a behaviour a stronger app could lack. Lesson 4 (simple gates) respected.
(3) Functional criteria (tests/scored/functional/judge.toml: 15 binary conjunctive criteria, total weight 61) require positive controls before crediting refusals (e.g. hro_moves line 40; hro_readonly_roles line 112 'if no kind has a successful control, this criterion is 0'; hro_candidate line 157 'A candidate page that receives none of its own data makes this criterion 0'), so a dead app cannot earn negative-only credit. Each polish row (tests/scored/polish/judge.toml:24-62) needs a working positive (update arrives within 60 s, re-send succeeds, draft returns after sign-in), so polish cannot be farmed by a non-working app. Visual likert is gated by the same browser gate (visual/prompt.md:101-104).
(4) Cross-criterion exemptions (functional/prompt.md:21 'Shared state', hro_activity line 94, hro_readonly_roles line 112) drop legs only when the sibling feature is broken. Under strict dominance (better app = worse app plus a correctly working feature) the better app passes the sibling criterion and every exempted leg, so no dominance inversion was found. Cascades (undo legs inside hro_reject_reopen and hro_interview_places; bulk inside hro_undo) raise the penalty for a missing feature but stay monotone (row 28 territory).
LATENT / UNMEASURED RISKS:
(a) Whole-suite timeout inversion: tests/test.sh run_suite (lines ~202-224) leaves reward 0 if the scored suite exceeds 11100 s. The task-chosen functional mode = 'individual' (functional/judge.toml:3) runs 15 sessions at timeout 600 (9000 s) plus polish 900 and visual 900 = 10800 s worst case, leaving about 300 s for 17 judge start-ups. A complete app forces the judge through every leg (slow); a broken app fails fast. If the suite overruns, a better app scores 0 while a worse one scores > 0, which is a ranking inversion. Per-criterion timeouts (NOT EXERCISED -> 0) can likewise cost a working app what a broken app forfeits anyway, and hro_readonly_roles has fewer replays when sibling kinds are broken. No full configured judge run exists to measure this.
(b) Fallback asymmetry: functional/prompt.md:21 lets an app with NO job-opening UI use the seeded Product Designer job (interview_limit 3) with places read relative to its state, while an app whose job form exists but mis-saves interview places is graded on its own wrong-capacity jobs and can lose hro_interview_places (5.5) and hro_bulk (5) as well as hro_intake_restart. Not a strict-dominance inversion (both apps carry a defect), so recorded as a note.
(c) Lesson 2 instance: every judge.toml carries the comment 'Criterion weights: 1.0 standard, 1.5 important, 2.0 core to the brief' (functional/judge.toml:23), but the functional weights are 2, 3, 3.5, 4, 4.5, 5 and 5.5, so the documented scheme is not the one used, and the weights do not obviously track brief importance (hro_two_people, the brief's 'hard part', is 4 against hro_long_thread 5.5). Between non-dominating apps the ranking depends on these undocumented weights, and an equal-weight recomputation can flip pairs. Weight honesty belongs to row 44; for row 42 it is not a demonstrated inversion.
RUNTIME EVIDENCE: qc/runs/hireops-lessons-2026-10-08-r5/raw-evidence-index.json (all 8 listed artifact hashes re-verified as matching) states 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' The scripted golden harness is not ranking evidence. qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md requires a hash-bound reward-ordering record before local clearance; none exists, so risk remains true. No Oracle, model or portal score is claimed.
counterexample: Not a demonstrated counterexample (verdict Note). Plausible inversion vector to measure: App B implements every feature correctly, so the configured judge walks all legs of 15 individual functional sessions and approaches the 600 s per-criterion and 11100 s scored-suite budgets; if the suite overruns, test.sh leaves reward 0. App A lacks undo and bulk; its sessions fail or exempt legs early, the suite finishes, and it scores > 0, outscoring B.
suggested_fix: Before clearance, produce the missing hash-bound reward-ordering record: run the full configured verifier on the golden and at least two mutated weaker apps (for example undo removed, or a job form that ignores interview places), confirm the golden outscores each mutant, and confirm the scored suite finishes well inside 11100 s. Also make the weight-scheme comment match the actual functional weights (or document their basis) without retuning weights to steer the band.
